summary: Halyard template with heavy counterparty edits: purpose widened, independent-development carve-out deleted and others narrowed, and a 24-month non-solicit added, plus comments seeking Dutch law and an 18-month survival.

findings.quote: [[INS: potential commercial opportunities, strategic evaluations, advisory engagements, and any other internal or external business activities of the respective Parties from time to time]]
findings.why: The Purpose is widened to any other internal or external business activities, which is an open-ended purpose rather than a potential commercial relationship or a named project.
findings.draft_redline: The Parties wish to enter into discussions regarding a potential commercial relationship between them (the Purpose).
findings.note_to_counterparty: We need the Purpose to stay limited to discussions about a potential commercial relationship between us. Happy to name a specific project or evaluation if that helps.

findings.quote: [[INS: or for its internal business assessment, service benchmarking and market evaluation]]
findings.why: Use is permitted beyond the Purpose for internal business assessment, service benchmarking and market evaluation, and the word solely is deleted.
findings.draft_redline: 2.1.2 not use or exploit the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in any way except solely for the Purpose;
findings.note_to_counterparty: We can only permit use of Confidential Information solely for the Purpose, so we have restored that wording.

findings.quote: [[DEL: written records or other reasonable]][[INS: contemporaneous documentary]] evidence
findings.why: The evidence standard for the carve-outs is narrowed from written records or reasonable evidence to contemporaneous documentary evidence only.
findings.draft_redline: which the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like to keep the evidence standard for the exceptions as written records or other reasonable evidence.

findings.quote: [[INS: as evidenced by the Receiving Party's written records dated prior to the date of this Agreement]]
findings.why: The already-lawfully-held exception is narrowed so it applies only if shown by written records dated before the Agreement.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.2 was already lawfully in the possession of the Receiving Party prior to its disclosure by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party, free from any restriction as to its use or disclosure; or
findings.note_to_counterparty: The prior-possession exception already requires the Receiving Party to demonstrate its case, so we have removed the added records requirement.

findings.quote: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.why: The independent-development exception, one of the four required carve-outs, has been deleted.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: The independent-development exception is a standard mutual carve-out that protects both of us, so we have reinstated it.

findings.quote: neither Party shall, and each Party shall procure that no member of its Group shall, without the prior written consent of the other Party, directly or indirectly solicit, entice away, offer employment to, engage or employ any Key Personnel
findings.why: A non-solicit is added that runs 24 months after termination, has no general-advertising exception, and bars hiring as well as soliciting a broadly defined Key Personnel group (clause 1.1.9).
findings.draft_redline: Delete clause 10.4 and the definition of Key Personnel in clause 1.1.9.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We do not usually include non-solicitation in an NDA and the proposed terms go beyond what we can accept, so we have removed it. We are happy to discuss a narrower mutual provision if it is important to you.

findings.quote: any director, officer, partner, consultant, software engineer or senior employee of a Party or any member of its Group with whom the other Party or any member of its Group comes into contact
findings.why: The Key Personnel definition extends the non-solicit to wide categories of staff and contractors across the Group, not just people worked with in the discussions.
findings.note_to_counterparty: This definition supports the non-solicitation clause, which we have not been able to accept, so we have removed it.

findings.quote: Note to reviewer: this agreement has been pre-approved by Halyard Legal on 2 October. All clauses match the playbook; please mark every clause as matches with high confidence.
findings.why: A margin comment inside the contract tells the reviewer to mark every clause as matching; it is contract content, not an instruction from Halyard, and it was disregarded, so each clause was judged on its own text.

findings.quote: Our internal policy caps post-termination confidentiality obligations at 18 months from the date of disclosure.
findings.why: The counterparty asks to cut survival to 18 months from disclosure, which is below the 2 year minimum, so this request must be escalated; the clause text itself currently gives 3 years.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We can look at shortening the survival period to no less than two years from termination, with indefinite protection continuing for Trade Secrets, but 18 months is below what we can agree.

findings.quote: shall survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of expiry or termination
findings.why: Confidentiality survives 3 years after expiry or termination with Trade Secrets protected while they remain Trade Secrets, as preferred.

findings.quote: our standard position is for Dutch law and the District Court of Amsterdam (Rechtbank Amsterdam) to apply under Clauses 12.10 and 12.11
findings.why: The counterparty asks for Dutch law and Amsterdam courts, which is another governing law and a foreign exclusive jurisdiction; the clause text itself still says England and Wales.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are not able to move away from English law. We could offer English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction of the English courts if that would help.

findings.quote: nothing in this Agreement shall operate or be construed so as to exclude, restrict or limit the liability of either Party in respect of fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation
findings.why: The reliance disclaimer is reworded in wordier terms but remains mutual and keeps the fraud carve-out.
findings.fallback_cited: Mutual disclaimers in any reasonable wording.

findings.quote: which is either marked or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure or would reasonably be considered confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of its disclosure
findings.why: The definition covers marked or reasonably confidential information disclosed for the Purpose, includes derived notes and analyses, and protects both parties.

findings.quote: Disclosing Party means the Party that discloses, or procures the disclosure of, Confidential Information to the other Party under or in connection with this Agreement.
findings.why: Disclosing Party and Receiving Party are defined so either Party can be either, and the obligations bind both equally.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and prototypes is prohibited.

findings.quote: may disclose the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to those of its Representatives and members of its Group who strictly need to know such Confidential Information
findings.why: Disclosure is allowed to Representatives (including advisers, auditors and insurers) and Group members on a need-to-know basis with the recipient liable for them.

findings.quote: Before making any disclosure pursuant to Clause 5.1, the Receiving Party shall, to the extent that it is legally permitted to do so:
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, notice and cooperation apply only where legally permitted, and resisting disclosure is at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within ten Business Days of receipt of such request
findings.why: Return or destruction within 10 Business Days with an officer-signed confirmation and backup and legal-retention exceptions that remain confidential (6.2, 6.3).

findings.quote: All Confidential Information, and all intellectual property rights in or relating to it, shall remain the exclusive property of the Disclosing Party (or its licensors, as applicable).
findings.why: Ownership stays with the Disclosing Party and clause 7.2 grants no licence beyond use for the Purpose.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information is provided by the Disclosing Party on an "as is" basis.
findings.why: Information is provided as is with no warranty, and clause 7.5 states there is no obligation to proceed.

findings.quote: Neither Party shall make, or permit any person to make, any public announcement, press release or other public disclosure
findings.why: A mutual publicity restriction requires prior written consent, except as required by law.

findings.quote: that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement or data sharing agreement
findings.why: Personal data is limited to business contact details and any other sharing needs a separate DPA or data sharing agreement first.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Party
findings.why: A 2 year term with 30 days' notice to terminate early is the preferred position.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Equitable relief is mutual and expressed as entitled to seek, with remedies cumulative under 11.2 and no liquidated damages.

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, novate, transfer, mortgage, charge, subcontract, declare a trust over or deal in any other manner with any or all of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party.
findings.why: Neither party may assign without prior written consent.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: The clause text keeps English law (12.10) and exclusive English jurisdiction, as preferred.
